scope: R191: FA tile sweep - shape tuning is worth at most 9 percent, not the 1.5x needed
numeric_equivalence_note: changing the tile changes accumulation order, so these outputs are NOT numerically equivalent to the default; this is measurement only and may never be a candidate

method.patched_private_copy: _build's br_cap/bc_cap made overridable via H3_FA_BR_CAP/H3_FA_BC_CAP, defaults untouched at 128/304
method.shape: B=1 H=7 N=41792 D=128 (the real FA shape)
method.per_config: separate process with separate TIK compile, warmup 2, 5 timed reps

validation: the 128/304 baseline of 154.57 ms matches the known 7.454 s / 50 blocks = 149 ms, so the measurement method is sound

conclusion.tile_tuning_ceiling: about 9 percent, far short of the 1.50x the 10 s target needs
conclusion.revealed_pattern: larger Bc means fewer tiles and less total time; Bc=128 needs about 2.4x the tiles and costs 1.65x the time
conclusion.interpretation: this is the signature of a sizeable fixed per-tile cost, matching R190's bubble conclusion: the problem is not that a 304-wide tile wastes cube work (384 is only 9 percent better) but that each tile pays a fixed cost
conclusion.implication: reducing the number of tiles and overlapping the per-tile dependency chain matter more than making one tile more efficient

for_the_10s_path.note: Bc=384 and better overlap are additive, so 384 is a sensible starting parameter for any new kernel

limits: Bc larger than 384 was not tried; UB capacity may not allow it and that needs checking separately
the bubble hypothesis is still only indirectly supported; an occupancy timeline has not been captured
output_sum differs across configs, which both confirms the rounding difference and rules out treating any of these as an equivalent implementation
